title: Cross-hand grip-change discordance has baseline-dependent DSST prediction gains across NHANES cycles
abstract: Among 1245 NHANES 2011–2012 adults aged 60+ and 1397 separately sampled 2013–2014 adults, we tested cross-hand discordance in first-to-third grip-strength changes. A frozen weighted spline-ridge model added this single feature to demographics, body size, maximal and mean strength, asymmetry, dispersion and common change. Source group-cross-validated MSE fell 0.21%, but target DSST MSE rose from 157.973 to 158.950 (+0.62%). Source-and-target PSU-refit bootstrap limits for the MSE difference were [-0.939, 4.745]. A post-hoc conventional strength/asymmetry baseline instead showed a 0.71% target MSE reduction with opposite feature coefficient. Dependence on baseline representation, uncertain estimates and historical dataset reuse preclude a robust incremental biomarker claim. This is cross-sectional prediction of a cognitive test score, not diagnosis or cognitive decline.
